title: Morning Edition
notes: Morning Edition for Sunday, Nov 8, 2026. It covers developments since Saturday’s Morning Edition, with ongoing stories marked with their earlier dates.

The lead is Saturday’s mass shooting in Kraków’s Main Market Square. Top stories: Trump’s call for a Justice Department probe of Democrats, the CFL division finals that set up the Grey Cup, defective columns at the unfinished Tung Chung West MTR station, the Communist Party’s delegate selection for its 2027 congress, and Gadi Eisenkot’s chance to form Israel’s next government.

China and World have five stories each; the U.S., Canada and Hong Kong have four, because this weekend’s fresh news there was thinner and we did not pad. Culture appears in the U.S. (SNL), Hong Kong (M+ anniversary) and China (Bingling grottoes exhibition); sports in Canada (CFL), China (trampoline worlds) and World (Paris Masters). Canada has no culture story this morning.
The Paris Masters final and Eisenkot’s formal appointment were scheduled for Sunday and are described as planned.
provenance: Stories are compiled from the linked sources; labels describe the type of claim each story rests on.
Source pages were opened during this morning’s research; the logged check time (6:25 AM ET) was recorded for the whole research batch rather than per page.

Xinhua and CGTN items are labelled State media. SCMP pages were partly paywalled; only their opening text was read. Two pages (an SCMP item and a Globe and Mail report) were read only from search excerpts, and one Xinhua explainer was not opened in full; this is noted on each. AP pages timed out in our fetch and were not relied on directly.
Several U.S. and Canadian items rest on a single outlet and are marked so in their source notes. New Zealand seat totals are preliminary.

stories.headline: Gunman kills six in Kraków’s Main Market Square in what Poland’s prime minister calls terrorism
stories.deck: A gunman driving through Kraków’s historic Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon fired at random people, killing six and injuring 16, police said. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it a terrorist attack.
stories.summary: A gunman driving through Kraków’s historic Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon fired at random people, killing six and injuring 16, police said. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it a terrorist attack. Police say the attack began shortly before 3 p.m. local time and lasted about three minutes; officers chased the car until it crashed, then shot and arrested the suspect, a 25-year-old Polish man who is in hospital after surgery. Four women and two men were killed — three Polish, one British and two not yet identified, according to the police chief — and five of the injured are foreign nationals. Two police officers were wounded, one critically. Tusk said three more bodies, two women and a man, were found at the suspect’s home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, with “strong indications” they were his immediate family. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the suspect appeared “fascinated by far-right ideologies” and held “ultra-nationalist” views. Kraków declared mourning until Nov. 11.
stories.why: Mass shootings are rare in Poland, and an attack on one of Europe’s busiest tourist squares by a suspect officials link to far-right ideas will put extremism and gun access at the centre of Polish and EU security debates.
stories.label: Reported + official statement
stories.note: Details such as the suspect’s motive come from Polish officials and are not yet established in court. The suspect has not been officially named. BBC reports mourning in Kraków until Nov. 11; DW reports Tusk announced two days of national mourning.

stories.headline: Herzog picks Gadi Eisenkot over Netanyahu to try to form Israel’s next government
stories.deck: Israel’s president said Saturday he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government, with the formal appointment set for a ceremony on Sunday in Jerusalem.
stories.summary: Israel’s president said Saturday he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government, with the formal appointment set for a ceremony on Sunday in Jerusalem. Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party and a former military chief of staff, will have 28 days to assemble 61 votes, with a possible 14-day extension; if no one succeeds, Israel faces fresh elections. His bloc won 48 seats in the Oct. 27 election to 53 for Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp, leaving neither with a majority. The Guardian reports both Arab-majority lists endorsed Eisenkot in consultations, but it is unclear whether his bloc would accept their support. “Now is the time to form a national emergency government,” Eisenkot wrote on X.
stories.why: If Eisenkot succeeds, Netanyahu — Israel’s longest-serving prime minister — would be out of office, a shift with consequences for Gaza, the West Bank and U.S.–Israel relations.
stories.label: Reported + official statement
stories.note: Ongoing story: earlier Donna Daily editions (Nov 4, 5 and 6) covered Herzog’s consultations. The formal ceremony was scheduled for Sunday afternoon in Jerusalem and had not taken place when this edition was compiled.

stories.headline: New Zealand’s photo-finish election leaves the next government unclear until special votes are counted
stories.deck: Preliminary results from New Zealand’s general election give National 42 seats to Labour’s 36, though Labour narrowly leads the party vote; neither leader claimed victory.
stories.summary: Preliminary results from New Zealand’s general election give National 42 seats to Labour’s 36, though Labour narrowly leads the party vote (29.3% to 29.2%, per the Guardian); neither leader claimed victory. On current numbers the right-leaning bloc of National, ACT and NZ First could form a majority, but about 400,000 special votes — overseas voters and those who voted outside their electorate — are still to be counted, with official results due Nov. 27. A large overhang could expand parliament to around 131 seats, RNZ says, and the new Opportunity party crossed the 5% threshold. RNZ notes six electorates are separated by fewer than 1,000 votes.
stories.why: Special votes have historically shifted a few seats toward the left, so a handful of close races could decide whether Christopher Luxon keeps power or a Labour-led bloc takes over.
stories.label: Reported + analysis
stories.note: Preliminary figures only; seat totals can change when special votes are counted. RNZ’s special-vote scenarios are modelling, not predictions.

stories.headline: Paraguay’s ousted president Santiago Peña charged and ordered held before trial over the Ueno bank collapse
stories.deck: A day after his removal from office, a judge ordered former president Santiago Peña held in pretrial detention at a military facility after prosecutors charged him with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, Reuters reported.
stories.summary: A day after his removal from office, a judge ordered former president Santiago Peña held in pretrial detention at a military facility after prosecutors charged him with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, Reuters reported. Prosecutors allege Peña used his office to keep large amounts of public money at the digital lender Ueno while he had financial ties to it; he was a shareholder in its holding company until 2025. His lawyer said Peña pleads not guilty. Former central bank chief Carlos Carvallo, who previously ran Ueno, was also charged and ordered detained. The Guardian reports the bank’s suspension froze the accounts of about 2.9 million people. The central bank said about $160 million had been paid to nearly 1.2 million savers under the deposit guarantee.
stories.why: The charges move Paraguay’s banking crisis from a political ouster to a criminal case against a man who was president until Friday, while millions of savers still wait for access to their money.
stories.label: Reported + allegation
stories.note: Ongoing story: the Nov 7 edition covered Peña’s removal and Pedro Alliana’s swearing-in. The allegations have not been tested in court; Peña denies wrongdoing. Reports differ on the exact share-sale date (Reuters: until March 2025; Guardian: April 2025).

stories.headline: Trump says he is ordering a Justice Department probe of Democrats he accuses of “extortion”
stories.deck: President Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to investigate Democratic leaders he accused of threatening officials and donors, without identifying the alleged letters or offering evidence, CNBC reported.
stories.summary: President Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to investigate Democratic leaders he accused of threatening officials and donors, without identifying the alleged letters or offering evidence, CNBC reported. In a Truth Social post he called Democrats’ talk of impeachment and investigations “extortion at the highest level” and singled out Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan. Slotkin replied that anyone who breaks the law or uses taxpayer money to enrich themselves should be held accountable — “If you didn’t break the law, then it’s all good.” CNBC notes a federal grand jury previously declined to indict Slotkin and other Democrats over a 2025 video. The same day, Trump posted that he had offered the White House press secretary job to UFC chief Dana White, NBC News reported, and CBS released a clip from a “60 Minutes” interview with Trump scheduled to air Sunday.
stories.why: Days after losing both chambers, Trump is answering Democrats’ promised oversight with threats of prosecution — a preview of the confrontation likely when the new Congress opens in January.
stories.label: Claim + official statement + reported
stories.note: Trump’s accusations are claims; no investigation, letters or evidence had been made public. Whether the Justice Department acts on the post is unknown.

stories.headline: Justice Department drops its bid to make California set aside about 20,000 ballots
stories.deck: The Justice Department moved Friday to dismiss its own lawsuit seeking to stop California from counting roughly 20,000 ballots it alleged went to noncitizens, a week before a court hearing on its list.
stories.summary: The Justice Department moved Friday to dismiss its own lawsuit seeking to stop California from counting roughly 20,000 ballots it alleged went to noncitizens, a week before a court hearing on its list. The motion said the relief it wanted was “no longer available” because the ballots would be mixed with lawful ones by then. California officials had said the list was out of date and included legitimate voters, and the case had already lost at the Ninth Circuit, in district court and at the Supreme Court. Attorney General Rob Bonta said the administration “chose to drop its case” rather than face scrutiny at the Nov. 13 evidentiary hearing. About 5 million California ballots were still uncounted as of Friday, AP reported.
stories.why: The retreat removes the most prominent federal challenge to a state’s midterm count, though the Justice Department is still litigating over its noncitizen lists and an Alaska case.

stories.headline: NYC Council calls an emergency hearing on lithium-ion battery fires after two blazes kill 10
stories.deck: The New York City Council will hold an emergency oversight hearing on Nov. 20 on lithium-ion battery fire safety after fires in the Bronx and Brooklyn’s Sunset Park killed 10 people within a week, the New York Daily News reported.
stories.summary: The New York City Council will hold an emergency oversight hearing on Nov. 20 on lithium-ion battery fire safety after fires in the Bronx and Brooklyn’s Sunset Park killed 10 people within a week, the New York Daily News reported. Four members of a Bronx family died after an e-bike battery exploded in their Mott Haven apartment on Oct. 28; six people died in a Sunset Park house fire on Thursday, where two lithium-ion batteries were found but the cause is still under investigation. Speaker Julie Menin called the rise in residential fires “an issue we must address.” FDNY figures cited in the report show 401 battery-linked fires so far this year, up from 292 in all of 2025, and 86 fire deaths citywide to date.
stories.why: E-bikes are how many New Yorkers get around and earn a living, so the Council’s next steps on charging, storage and enforcement will reach far beyond the families affected.
stories.label: Reported + official figures
stories.note: The cause of the Sunset Park fire had not been determined in the report. Some figures in the article appear inconsistent (for example on injuries), so only the clearly stated totals are used here.

stories.headline: Poilievre pans the budget’s $15-million capital gains exemption as too narrow
stories.deck: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre said the federal budget’s proposed $15-million capital gains exemption for founders excludes so many sectors that he can’t figure out “who actually qualifies,” in an interview airing Sunday.
stories.summary: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre said the federal budget’s proposed $15-million capital gains exemption for founders excludes so many sectors that he can’t figure out “who actually qualifies,” in an interview airing Sunday on CBC’s Rosemary Barton Live. The Canada Growth Incentive excludes sectors including agriculture, fishing, finance, real estate, food and accommodation, and arts and entertainment; the budget puts its cost at $715 million over four years. Poilievre backed the budget’s productivity “mega-deduction” but pitched letting people defer tax on capital gains reinvested in Canada. NDP Leader Avi Lewis said the budget favours CEOs and investors; Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said a third of new revenue goes to support people.
stories.why: How the opposition parties line up on the budget’s tax measures matters for whether Prime Minister Mark Carney’s minority government can pass it.

stories.headline: Hundreds rally across Nova Scotia against a planned AI data centre in Cape Breton
stories.deck: Protesters gathered in the rain in Halifax, Kentville, Port Hawkesbury and Truro on Saturday to oppose EverWind Fuels’ planned data centre at Point Tupper, CBC News reported.
stories.summary: Protesters gathered in the rain in Halifax, Kentville, Port Hawkesbury and Truro on Saturday to oppose EverWind Fuels’ planned data centre at Point Tupper, CBC News reported. The first phase, planned for next year, would support the AI company Anthropic’s chatbot Claude. Hundreds turned out at Province House in Halifax, with placards about water and electricity use; others raised Mi’kmaw consent. EverWind says it will draw power from the grid until its approved wind farms are built. The province said a data centre can only proceed if it meets federal and provincial guidelines on water, the environment and power rates, and that a potential $10-billion investment is worth being “open minded about.”
stories.why: Data centres for AI are arriving in smaller communities across North America, and Nova Scotia’s debate over water, power bills and Indigenous consent is a test case for who gets a say.

stories.headline: ER doctors say a veterinary sedative mixed into street fentanyl is complicating overdose care
stories.deck: Emergency physicians across Canada say medetomidine, a veterinary sedative not approved for humans, is turning up in street fentanyl and making overdoses and withdrawal harder to treat, CBC News reported.
stories.summary: Emergency physicians across Canada say medetomidine, a veterinary sedative not approved for humans, is turning up in street fentanyl and making overdoses and withdrawal harder to treat, CBC News reported. First detected in Canada in 2023, it has increased substantially in B.C. and Ontario and risen sharply this year in Saskatchewan and Yukon, according to the Canadian Centre on Substance Use and Addiction. Naloxone reverses opioids but not medetomidine, so responders are told to focus on breathing. Doctors describe severe withdrawal — racing heart, high blood pressure, vomiting, delirium — that can require hospital or intensive care. Some physicians called for more supervised consumption sites; Ontario’s health ministry pointed to its new treatment hubs instead.
stories.why: A new adulterant that naloxone can’t reverse changes the basic first-aid advice for overdoses and adds strain to already crowded emergency rooms.
stories.label: Reported

stories.headline: About 30 substandard columns found at the unfinished Tung Chung West MTR station
stories.deck: Hong Kong’s Buildings Department said around 30 substandard concrete columns have been found at the Tung Chung West station under construction, but that the defects pose no risk to the structure because temporary supports remain in place.
stories.summary: Hong Kong’s Buildings Department said around 30 substandard concrete columns have been found at the Tung Chung West station under construction, but that the defects pose no risk to the structure because temporary supports remain in place. The department said it first confirmed two defective columns during a routine audit on Oct. 27; more were found as concrete was removed and reported to it last week. It has asked the registered structural engineers to submit an investigation report and remedial plan by mid-November. The MTR Corporation has suspended the relevant works. A preliminary review found no evidence of intentional deviation from approved plans, the department said.

stories.headline: M+ marks five years with free entry to designated galleries on Sunday and a Hong Kong New Wave film festival
stories.deck: West Kowloon’s M+ museum scheduled free admission to designated exhibitions on Sunday, Nov. 8, closing an eight-day fifth-anniversary programme; it says it has drawn more than 12.5 million visits since opening in 2021.
stories.summary: West Kowloon’s M+ museum scheduled free admission to designated exhibitions on Sunday, Nov. 8 (10:00–20:00), closing an eight-day fifth-anniversary programme; it says it has drawn more than 12.5 million visits since opening in 2021. The two ticketed special exhibitions — “Design Ah!” and “Myths and Monsters: The Art of Fantasy in Asia” — are excluded. The anniversary also launched the first M+ Restored Festival, screening all nine restored Hong Kong New Wave films, with screenings and filmmaker talks continuing on selected weekends into December. The museum says about half its visitors are from Hong Kong and that it will launch an M+ Academy for cultural leaders this month.
stories.why: For film and theatre lovers, the restored New Wave series is a rare chance to see the movies that defined modern Hong Kong cinema on a big screen.

stories.headline: Three hikers, two of them teenagers, hurt after being hit by a landing paraglider in Ma On Shan Country Park
stories.deck: A woman and two boys were airlifted to hospital after a paraglider struck them while landing at the Ngong Ping campsite in Ma On Shan Country Park on Sunday, police said.
stories.summary: A woman and two boys were airlifted to hospital after a paraglider struck them while landing at the Ngong Ping campsite in Ma On Shan Country Park on Sunday, police said. Police received the report at about 12:36 p.m. from the 42-year-old woman; her 14-year-old son and a 15-year-old boy were also hit. The three suffered head and back injuries and were flown by the Government Flying Service to Ruttonjee Hospital in Wan Chai.
stories.why: Ma On Shan’s Ngong Ping plateau is a popular spot for both hikers and paragliders on autumn weekends, and the accident raises questions about how the shared space is managed.

stories.headline: China’s Communist Party starts choosing 2,360 delegates for its 21st congress in 2027
stories.deck: The Communist Party’s Central Committee issued a circular launching the election of 2,360 delegates to its 21st national congress, to be held in Beijing in the second half of 2027, Xinhua reported.
stories.summary: The Communist Party’s Central Committee issued a circular launching the election of 2,360 delegates to its 21st national congress, to be held in Beijing in the second half of 2027, Xinhua reported. Delegates will be chosen by 38 electoral units nationwide. The statement said Xi Jinping convened Politburo and Standing Committee meetings on the plan, and stressed “putting political standards first” and strict eligibility checks. A Xinhua explainer says the process runs through June 2027 and candidate lists must exceed seats by more than 15%.
stories.why: The congress, held every five years, sets the party’s top leadership; the delegate process is the first formal step toward a meeting that will show whether and how Xi signals a successor.

stories.summary: More than 600 expedition members departed Sanya on Saturday aboard the icebreakers Xuelong and Xuelong 2 and a third vessel, Xinhua reported, with a return planned for April 2027. stories.headline: Bingling Temple Grottoes treasures go on show in Lanzhou, most for the first time
stories.deck: An exhibition of 165 relics and sets of relics from the 1,600-year-old Bingling Temple Grottoes opened Saturday at the Gansu Jiandu Museum in Lanzhou, Xinhua reported.
stories.summary: An exhibition of 165 relics and sets of relics from the 1,600-year-old Bingling Temple Grottoes opened Saturday at the Gansu Jiandu Museum in Lanzhou, Xinhua reported. About two-thirds of the pieces are on public display for the first time, and the show runs until Feb. 7, 2027. The grottoes in Yongjing County, part of the UNESCO-listed Silk Roads network, contain 216 caves and niches, 815 statues and more than 900 square metres of murals.
stories.why: Cave art along the Silk Road is rarely moved; bringing it to a city museum lets far more people see Buddhist sculpture and murals that usually require a trip to a remote gorge.

stories.summary: China’s Zhang Yu, Zhu Xueying and Zhang Xinxin retained the women’s team title at the Trampoline World Championships in Nanjing on Saturday, while Belarus beat the hosts to the men’s crown, CGTN reported. Zhang Xinxin sealed it by edging Belarus’s Viyaleta Bardzilouskaya by 0.020 points in the final group; Russia took silver and Belarus bronze. In the men’s final, a landing error by two-time world champion Yan Langyu proved costly as Belarus won with 25 points to China’s 23.

stories.headline: China’s foreign exchange reserves edge up to $3.405 trillion at the end of October
stories.deck: China’s foreign exchange reserves rose by $4.9 billion in October to $3.4052 trillion, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange said.
stories.summary: China’s foreign exchange reserves rose by $4.9 billion in October to $3.4052 trillion, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange said, according to Xinhua — a 0.14% gain. The regulator attributed the rise to currency conversion and asset-price changes in a month when the U.S. dollar index rose and major asset prices were mixed.
stories.why: The world’s largest reserve pile gives Beijing room to steady the yuan ahead of trade talks with Washington and the APEC summit it hosts this month.
